title: Tractor Beam
description: Map a tractor beam by querying an Intcode drone, then find where a 100x100 square fits inside it.
writeup:
## Approach

Each query requires a fresh Intcode run, so efficiency matters. Part 1 is brute force. Part 2 exploits the beam's geometry — it expands monotonically, so we can scan rows top to bottom tracking the left edge.

## Part 1

Probe every point in the 50x50 grid and count how many return 1 (in the beam). Each probe is an independent Intcode execution with inputs `[x, y]`.

## Part 2

The beam forms a cone expanding from the origin. For each row `y`, find the leftmost `x` in the beam (tracking it as we go down since it only moves right). Then check if `(x + 99, y - 99)` is also in the beam — if so, there's a 100-wide beam span at row `y` and the beam extends at least 99 rows above at that right edge, meaning a 100x100 square fits with its top-left at `(x, y - 99)`. The answer is `x * 10000 + (y - 99)`.
